question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{x+3}+\sqrt{x+5}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{x+3}+\sqrt{x+5},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12}{\sqrt{x+3}-\sqrt{x+5}} & = \\ \frac{12}{\sqrt{x+3}-\sqrt{x+5}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{x+3}+\sqrt{x+5}}{\sqrt{x+3}+\sqrt{x+5}} & = \\ \frac{12(\sqrt{x+3}+\sqrt{x+5})}{(\sqrt{x+3}+\sqrt{x+5})(\sqrt{x+3}+\sqrt{x+5})} & = \\ \frac{12(\sqrt{x+3}+\sqrt{x+5})}{(\sqrt{x+3})^{2}-(\sqrt{x+5})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{12(\sqrt{x+3}+\sqrt{x+5})}{(x+3)-(x+5)} & = \\ \frac{12(\sqrt{x+3}+\sqrt{x+5})}{-2} & = \\ -6(\sqrt{x+3}+\sqrt{x+5})\end{aligned}
$$
